children: Japan’s core consumer price index, which excludes fresh food but includes energy, increased 1.7% year-on-year in August 2026, after a 1.8% rise in July.
The latest reading slowed from the highest rate in six months, touched a month earlier, and was below the market forecast of 1.8%.

Still, the latest reading remained below the Bank of Japan’s 2% target for an eighth straight month, as government fuel subsidies helped offset price pressures from higher oil costs linked to the Middle East conflict.

Meanwhile, the index excluding the effects of volatile fresh food and fuel, which the Bank of Japan closely watches as a better gauge of demand-driven price movements, stood at 1.9% year-on-year in August, remaining at the fastest increase in three months.
The BoJ left interest rates at 1.0% at its July meeting, keeping them at their highest level since September 1995, following a 25-bps hike in June to prevent higher oil prices from fueling inflation.

title: Japan Core Inflation Eases, Below Forecasts
